panel.title: RoomMind
panel.subtitle: Climate management
panel.no_areas: No areas configured in Home Assistant.
panel.no_areas_hint: Add areas in HA settings to get started.
badge.beta_hint: This feature is in beta and may change or be restructured in future updates.
room.control_mode.full_control_info: RoomMind has full control over your climate devices. An external temperature sensor provides the actual room temperature, enabling proportional setpoint calculation. The device setpoint is dynamically adjusted based on MPC power output. The thermal model (EKF) learns your room's behavior for optimal comfort and energy efficiency.
room.control_mode.managed_info: RoomMind sets the target temperature on your device (from schedule, override, or vacation settings), but the device self-regulates using its own internal sensor. No proportional boost, no thermal model learning, and no MPC optimization. For more precise control, assign an external temperature sensor in the Devices section.
room.outdoor_hint: Disables climate control, mold detection, and model training. Sensor monitoring continues.
override.label: Temporary Override
override.invalid_band: Cooling target must be at or above the heating target
hero.mpc_learning_paused.outdoor_unavail: RoomMind needs an outdoor temperature to learn this room's thermal model. The configured outdoor sensor is unavailable and no weather entity is set as a fallback. Configure either in Settings.
hero.compressor_protection_info: This room shares an outdoor compressor with other rooms. To prevent short-cycling, the shared compressor group enforces a minimum run time and a minimum off time before this device is allowed to switch again.
hero.coil_dry_info: The AC is running its evaporator drying cycle and switches off afterwards. Cooling demand cancels it immediately.
mode.auto_desc: Heats & cools automatically based on target temperature
mode.heat_only_desc: Heats only. With thermostats in the room, ACs stay off unless smart source selection is on
mode.cool_only_desc: Only uses ACs, thermostats stay off
schedule.selector_warning: Multiple schedules but no selector set. Only the first will be used.
schedule.preheat_hint: Turn off for rooms that should not warm up beforehand, e.g. a bedroom at night. Heating then starts only shortly before the block.
schedule.follow_device_setpoint_label: Take over changes made on the device
schedule.follow_device_setpoint_hint: Only for devices that report their setpoint to Home Assistant. Leave it off if a device or an automation changes the setpoint by itself (own schedule, frost or window protection).
schedule.help_temps_title: How is the target temperature determined?
schedule.help_temps: The target temperature follows this priority chain:
schedule.help_temps_1: Manual override – A temporary boost/eco/custom override always takes highest priority.
schedule.help_temps_2: Block temperature – If the active schedule block has a temperature value in its data, that value is used.
schedule.help_temps_3: Comfort temperature – If the schedule is "on" but the block has no temperature, the comfort fallback temperature below is used.
schedule.help_temps_4: Eco temperature – When the schedule is "off" (outside all time blocks), the eco temperature is used.
schedule.help_block: You can set a specific temperature for each time block by adding a temperature value in the schedule's YAML configuration:
schedule.help_block_note: If a block has no temperature data, the comfort fallback temperature is used instead.
schedule.help_split: For auto-mode rooms, you can set separate heating and cooling targets per time block using heat_temperature and cool_temperature:
schedule.help_split_note: If only one is set, the other falls back to the room's comfort temperature. These keys take priority over temperature when present.
schedule.help_multi: You can add multiple schedules and switch between them using a selector entity. This can be an input_boolean (toggles between schedule 1 and 2) or an input_number (selects by number). Without a selector entity, only the first schedule is used.
schedule.comfort_hint_auto: Comfort: target when schedule is on. Eco: target when schedule is off. Rows set the target for heating and cooling.
schedule.comfort_hint: Used when schedule is "on" but no temperature is set in the block
schedule.block_temp_rejected: Values outside the valid range {min}–{max}{unit}: {values}. The comfort target is used instead — check the schedule helper for a typo.
devices.no_climate: No climate entities found in this area.
devices.occupancy_sensor_hint: Improves thermal model accuracy by tracking room occupancy
devices.occupancy_eco: Eco when the room is empty
devices.heating_system_type_info: Radiators and especially underfloor heating keep giving off heat after they stop. RoomMind counts this afterglow and overshoots less. Underfloor heating also runs longer at a time.
devices.underfloor_delay_hint: Underfloor heating has long restart times. A window-open delay of at least 5 minutes is recommended to avoid unnecessary shutoffs.
devices.heating_system_type_boost_hint: Tip: If the heating system has changed, pick "Re-learn faster" for the room under Settings › Model Training.
devices.setback_auto_off: Turn off after an hour without demand
devices.coil_dry_global_off_hint: Evaporator drying is switched off globally, so nothing runs for this device. Turn it on in the settings, or set this device to "Always on".
devices.valve_closing_mode_hint: What the second value means. Most thermostats have a closing degree (SONOFF TRVZB: valve_closing_degree). The SONOFF TRV-ZBT has the valve opening while it does not heat instead (Zigbee2MQTT: idle_valve_position): pick "Opening while idle" there, or the valve stays open when the room needs no heat.
devices.info.types_body: Thermostat means a radiator thermostat / TRV. Climate Device means an AC, heat pump, or other climate entity used for cooling or forced-air heating. Both are Home Assistant climate entities; the distinction is how RoomMind controls them.
devices.info.control_body: Setpoint mode and offset exist for thermostats and climate devices in rooms with a temperature sensor. Proportional: RoomMind controls the output through the setpoint. Direct: the device regulates to the real target itself.
devices.info.modes_body: When idle, climate devices can turn off, run only the fan or stay in setback (setpoint 2 °C away from the room target). Thermostats turn off or stay awake on a low setpoint, for wireless thermostats that fall asleep when off.
devices.info.heat_source_body: This appears only when a room has both a thermostat/TRV and a Climate Device plus an external temperature sensor. RoomMind can then choose which source should handle heating based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
covers.auto_control_hint: RoomMind closes blinds when solar gain is predicted to overheat the room.
covers.deploy_threshold_hint: Close blinds when predicted temperature exceeds target by this amount.
covers.min_position_hint: Blinds will never close further than this (0 = fully closed allowed).
covers.override_minutes_hint: How long to pause automatic control after manual cover movement. Set to 0 for no pause.
covers.no_covers_in_area: No cover entities found in this area.
covers.night_close_hint: Automatically close covers at sunset and open at sunrise.
covers.window_hold_hint: While a window or door sensor of this room is open, RoomMind does not lower the covers and catches up once it is closed. For blinds that would hit an open window (inside blinds, roof windows). RoomMind checks every 30 seconds and does not stop a cover that is already moving.
covers.schedule_section_hint: Define time windows for cover control using HA schedule helpers. In Force position mode the schedule's position overrides solar/thermal logic. In Allow solar protection mode RoomMind decides the position within the active window.
covers.schedule_position_hint: Cover position when this schedule is active (0% = fully closed, 100% = fully open).
covers.schedule_selector_hint: Choose which schedule is active. input_boolean: off=#1, on=#2. input_number: value selects schedule number.
covers.schedule_selector_warning: Multiple schedules configured but no selector set. Only the first schedule will be used.
covers.night_position_hint: Cover position when night close is active (0% = fully closed). Covers with an individual min. position will never go below that.
covers.night_close_elevation_hint: How far below or above the horizon the sun must be. 0° = exactly at sunset/sunrise. Negative = darker (e.g. -6° = dusk, when it's noticeably dark). Positive = still bright (e.g. 5° = sun still visible above horizon).
covers.night_close_offset_hint: Additional shift relative to the sun position threshold. Positive = close later (e.g. +20 = 20 min after threshold is reached), negative = close earlier.
covers.outdoor_min_temp_hint: Don't close covers for solar protection below this outdoor temperature. Solar heat gain is welcome when it's cold.
covers.per_cover_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces and optional individual minimum positions.
covers.per_cover_min_position_hint: Individual minimum position per cover. Covers will never close further than this. Useful when blinds are physically fully closed at a position > 0%.
covers.snap_deploy_hint: Close covers directly to the minimum position instead of gradually closing. Recommended for triple-pane windows where intermediate positions can cause thermal stress.
covers.info.selection_body: Select covers/blinds from this area or add entities from other areas. RoomMind tracks their position and can control them automatically.
covers.info.schedule_body: Use HA schedule helpers to define times when covers should close (e.g. privacy in the evening). The schedule's position attribute determines how far they close. Schedules override all other automatic logic.
covers.info.solar_body: When automatic control is enabled, RoomMind predicts whether solar radiation will overheat the room and closes blinds preventively. It uses learned thermal data when available, otherwise a conservative default. The deploy threshold controls how much predicted overshoot is needed before blinds close.
covers.info.night_body: Closes covers at sunset and opens them at sunrise. You can set a custom night position (e.g. 10% = almost closed but not fully).
covers.info.override_body: If you manually move a cover, RoomMind detects this and pauses automatic control for the configured duration. This prevents fighting with the user.
covers.info.priority_body: Manual override > Schedule > Night close > Solar/thermal control. Higher priority rules always win. When no rule applies, covers stay open.
covers.info.entities_body: RoomMind creates two entities per room for external use: switch.roommind_{area}_cover_auto (enable/disable automatic cover control — usable in automations or dashboards) and binary_sensor.roommind_{area}_cover_paused (on when manual override is active, e.g. after manually moving a cover).
covers.orientation_hint: Set the compass direction each cover faces. RoomMind then shades only while the sun is actually on that side of the building. Without a direction, covers react to sunshine in general and may close from sunrise, even on a north window.
settings.climate_control_hint: When disabled, RoomMind continues to monitor all sensors and train the model, but sends no commands to your heating or cooling devices. Your devices keep their current mode and setpoint and may continue heating or cooling on their own. RoomMind will not turn them off.
settings.learning_hint: When paused, RoomMind stops collecting new measurement data and training the thermal model. Existing model data is preserved.
settings.learning_state.not_learning: Does not learn, the room has no temperature sensor of its own
settings.smart_control_hint: Configure outdoor temperature limits for heating and cooling.
settings.outdoor_cooling_min_hint: AC stays off when outdoor temperature is below this value. A manual override ignores this limit
settings.outdoor_heating_max_hint: Heating stays off when outdoor temperature exceeds this value. A manual override ignores this limit
settings.control_mode_hint: Intelligent: MPC learns each room's thermal behavior and plans ahead (on/off control while it is still learning). Simple: on/off control with hysteresis only; the model keeps learning in the background but does not make decisions, and automatic blinds use a simpler solar estimate instead of the MPC forecast.
settings.comfort_weight_hint: Balances temperature precision against energy use. Comfort reacts earlier and stays closer to target. Efficiency allows more drift to reduce heating/cooling runtime. At the default and above, rooms are heated up ahead of a schedule block so they are warm when it starts; below the default it starts later, at full efficiency only shortly before the block.
settings.preheat_lead: Pre-heats up to {time} before a warmer schedule block.
settings.preheat_lead_none: No pre-heating: heats only shortly before a warmer schedule block.
settings.weather_entity_hint: Optional: enables predictive outdoor temperature planning, and acts as a fallback when the outdoor sensor is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify: Notify when outdoor temperature is unavailable
settings.outdoor_unavailable_notify_hint: Show a Home Assistant notification when neither the outdoor sensor nor the weather entity has reported a temperature for 30 minutes. While this is the case, RoomMind pauses thermal model learning to avoid corruption.
settings.prediction_enabled_hint: Show predicted temperature trend in analytics charts. Disable if you experience slow performance.
vacation.title: Vacation Mode
vacation.hint: Sets all rooms to a setback temperature until the end date.
analytics.afterglow_sub: In this room it fades in about {time}.
analytics.afterglow_unmeasured: Not measured yet: RoomMind measures it after the next heating runs.
analytics.info.accuracy_idle: How far the model may be off when it predicts the room temperature 5 minutes ahead while nothing heats or cools. It is the model's own estimate, not a measurement, and once the model has learned it settles at about ±{typical} in most homes. It says nothing about how closely the room is kept at its target, that is what "This period" above shows. Below ±{threshold} RoomMind uses its predictive control.
analytics.info.accuracy_heating: The same while heating. It stays higher at first because the model needs real heating runs to learn from. Once heating and idle are below ±{threshold}, RoomMind switches from simple on/off control to predictive control. Overshoot after heating comes from how slowly the heating reacts, not from this value.
analytics.info.confidence: How well the model knows the room: enough readings while idle and while heating or cooling, and how accurately it predicts. Around 50 % it usually still lacks heating or cooling runs. Predictive control starts once enough runs are measured and the prediction is within ±{threshold}, which can be below 80 %.
analytics.comfort_pending: Time on target appears here once RoomMind has recorded targets for this room.
analytics.rhythm_hint: Click a date or a cell to show that day above, point at a cell to see the hour.
analytics.rhythm_hint_touch: Tap a date to show that day above, a cell to see the hour.
analytics.info.summary: On target means the room was at most {tolerance} below its heating target or above its cooling target. A room that only heats can only be too cold, one that only cools only too warm. Times with an open window do not count. Runs come from one reading every 3 to 5 minutes, so very short runs can be missing. After a heating run the room often keeps warming for a while: "then avg." is how far it went past the target the run heated for within the hour after it. A pre-heat run counts against the coming target (cooling likewise below the target).
analytics.info.heat_loss: How fast the room cools down without heating at the difference to outside shown above (twice that difference means twice the loss). A lower value means a better insulated room. To compare a renovation, look at this value before and after. Learned from the room's own behaviour; shown per hour because the model does not know the size of the room, so it cannot give watts.
analytics.info.time_constant: In this time the room, without heating, covers almost two thirds of the way to the outdoor temperature. Longer means better insulated.
analytics.info.heating_rate: How fast the heating warms the room at full power, in degrees per hour. RoomMind uses it to work out when to start heating.
analytics.info.cooling_rate: How fast the AC cools the whole room, walls and furniture included, at full power. The model handles separately that the air at the sensor drops faster at first and springs back after the stop.
analytics.info.afterglow: How much warmer a 10-minute heating run still makes the room after it stops, because the radiators have stored heat, and how long that takes to fade. RoomMind measures this after every run and stops heating earlier to match. If it is large, the room heats in shorter steps so it does not overshoot.
analytics.info.solar_gain: How fast the sun warms the room on a clear summer noon. What arrives right now and at most today is shown below; in winter it is often a quarter. RoomMind heats less when sun is coming. The tile appears once the model has seen sun.
analytics.info.occupancy_gain: How much warmer the room gets per hour while an occupancy sensor reports it occupied (people, devices). Learned from the occupied times; until then a dash shows here.
analytics.info.data_points: Readings the model has learned from. About one is added every 3 minutes.
settings.intro.orphans: Rooms whose Home Assistant area was deleted. RoomMind no longer controls them but keeps their settings and what they learned.
settings.orphans_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" with its settings and learned data?
settings.reset_hint: Clear learned thermal model data and history. The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_all_hint: Clear thermal data and history for all rooms at once.
settings.reset_all_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for ALL rooms? All models will start learning from scratch.
settings.reset_room_hint: Select a room to clear its thermal data and history.
settings.reset_room_confirm: Clear all learned thermal data and history for this room? The model will start learning from scratch.
settings.boost_hint: After a bigger change in a room, like a new radiator, an AC or new insulation, choose the graduation cap icon next to the room. New measurements then count more until the next heating or cooling runs are measured, and the model usually takes on the change with those runs. Without the nudge this usually takes up to a day. For a complete fresh start:
settings.boost_confirm:
Re-learn {room} faster?

New measurements count more until the next heating or cooling runs are measured. This cannot be undone.
learning.boost_info: After "Re-learn faster" new measurements count more for a while, so the model picks up a change in the room sooner. It fades by itself. The time left is an estimate, it only runs while the room learns (window closed, outdoor temperature known).
analytics.chart_info_body:
**Lines:** The solid line is the measured room temperature, the green dashed line the target in force. Where something other than the schedule set it, it changes colour: pink for an override, grey-blue when nobody was home, on vacation or the room was empty, brown for mould protection; the tooltip names the reason. Right of the now line: target and prediction (dotted) for the next 3 hours, using the weather forecast if one is set up.

**Target range:** The figures above count the pale green band as on target: from {tolerance} below the heating target up to {tolerance} above the cooling target (heat only: everything from the heating side up, cool only: everything from the cooling side down). Below it is tinted pale blue (too cold), above it pale red (too warm).

**Strip and areas:** The strip along the bottom shows when the room heated (orange) or cooled (blue), a grey area an open window.

**Below:** Outdoor temperature; humidity with a green band for 40–60 % (line yellow at 30–40 and 60–70 %, red beyond; too dry irritates the airways, too humid favours mould on cold walls); electricity price in the source's unit when the room follows the price: green cheap, grey normal, red expensive.
presence.title: Presence Detection
presence.hint: Uses eco temperature when nobody is home.
presence.hint_detail: When enabled, all rooms switch to eco temperature as soon as none of the configured persons are home. You can optionally restrict per room which persons are relevant.
presence.room_help_body: Select which persons are relevant for this room. The room switches to eco temperature when none of the selected persons are home. Without selection, the global rule applies: eco when nobody is home.
presence.room_none_assigned: Everyone counts: eco when nobody is home
presence.missing_entity_hint: This entity no longer exists in Home Assistant. Remove it to clear it from this room.
presence.help_ignore_body: When enabled, this room skips presence detection entirely. It always follows its schedule and never switches to eco based on who is home. Useful for rooms that should maintain temperature regardless of presence, such as a server room, a pet room, or a guest room used by someone not tracked by Home Assistant.
presence.tile_ignored: Presence detection is ignored. Room always follows its schedule.
presence.clears_override_hint: When nobody is home, manual overrides are paused and the room follows the away action. When someone returns, the override resumes until it expires.
presence.room_disabled: Presence detection is turned off in the settings. What you set here only takes effect once it is on there.
presence.room_no_persons: No person is set up in the settings yet. Until then no room switches to eco because nobody is home.
presence.ignore_info: The room never switches to eco because nobody is home. For example a guest room or a room that should always stay warm.
presence.persons_info: The room switches to eco when none of these people is home. Without a choice everyone from the settings counts.
valve_protection.title: Valve Protection
valve_protection.hint: Periodically opens idle TRV valves briefly to prevent seizing or calcification.
valve_protection.interval_hint: How long a valve can be idle before being cycled (1–90 days)
compressor.title: Compressor Protection
compressor.members_hint: Select all climate devices powered by this compressor (indoor splits, TRVs on radiators, fan coils).
compressor.draft_no_members: Saved once it has an indoor unit.
compressor.min_run_hint: Compressor must run at least this long once started.
compressor.min_off_hint: Compressor must stay off at least this long after stopping.
compressor.master_entity_hint: The central unit that powers the indoor devices in this group, e.g. a gas boiler, outdoor heat pump unit, or ducted AC master switch. RoomMind will turn it on when any room needs heating or cooling, and off when all rooms are idle. Leave empty to use only the action script or short-cycle protection.
compressor.conflict_resolution_hint: Determines what happens when some rooms need heating while others need cooling at the same time. Heating priority: heating always wins (safest for frost protection). Cooling priority: cooling always wins. Majority: the mode with more rooms wins, ties go to heating. Outdoor temperature: uses the outdoor heating max threshold from settings to decide automatically.
compressor.action_script_hint: A Home Assistant script that runs whenever the heating/cooling demand changes. Useful for systems that need special commands, e.g. cancelling a Vaillant Quick Veto or toggling a relay. Works with or without a master device. Without a master device, only the script is triggered. Receives variables: action (heat/cool/idle), master_entity, members, active_members.
compressor.enforce_uniform_mode_hint: All thermostats in this group must operate in the same HVAC mode (all heating or all cooling). Rooms that disagree with the resolved group mode will be set to idle. Use this for heat pumps that start automatically but require all connected units to run the same mode.
coil_dry.title: Evaporator drying
coil_dry.hint: After cooling, keep the indoor fan running for a while before the AC really switches off. Dries the evaporator so no biofilm forms and the next start does not smell musty.
coil_dry.duration_hint: How long the fan keeps running (1–60 min). At a low fan speed allow roughly twice as long as at a high one.
coil_dry.min_cooling_hint: Only dry after the AC has cooled for at least this long. Short cooling bursts are added up (1–240 min).
coil_dry.mode_dry_warning: In dry mode the compressor keeps running and cools the coil down again, which works against drying. Only pick this if your unit's dry mode is mostly fan.
coil_dry.fan_mode_hint: A higher speed dries faster but is louder. Speeds the device does not report are skipped — it then keeps its current one.
coil_dry.drain_hint: Leave the AC off first so condensate can drain, then start the fan (0–15 min). Reduces how much moisture is blown back into the room.
mold.title: Mold Risk Protection
mold.detection_desc: Receive notifications when humidity indicates mold risk
mold.threshold_hint: Alert when room humidity stays above this value
mold.insulation_hint: Used to estimate how cold the coldest spot of your exterior walls gets (corners, window reveals). If unsure, keep Standard. Needs an outdoor temperature.
mold.sustained_hint: Alert only after risk persists for this long
mold.prevention_desc: Automatically raise temperature to reduce mold risk
mold.intensity_hint: Warmer air reduces surface humidity on cold walls. Light is usually sufficient for moderate risk, Strong can lower surface humidity by up to 8–10% — but uses noticeably more energy.
settings.intro.general: Master switch for climate control and how the room overview is arranged.
settings.intro.sensors: Configure outdoor sensors and weather data for accurate climate control.
settings.intro.control: Choose how RoomMind controls your climate devices and set priority and thresholds.
settings.intro.presence: Automatically reduce temperature when nobody is home.
settings.intro.vacation: Set all rooms to a reduced temperature while you are away.
settings.intro.valve: Periodically move idle TRV valves to prevent seizing or calcification.
settings.intro.compressor: Indoor units that share an outdoor unit or heat source: minimum run and pause times prevent rapid on/off switching.
settings.intro.mold: Monitor humidity and automatically reduce mold risk.
settings.intro.notifications: Configure who receives alerts and how.
settings.intro.learning: How far each room's model is, pause learning and re-learn faster after changes.
settings.intro.reset: Clear learned thermal model data. The model will start learning from scratch.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.enabled_hint: When disabled, no notifications are sent — neither to devices nor to the HA sidebar.
notifications.desc: Choose which devices receive alerts. Without targets, alerts appear in the HA sidebar.
notifications.add_target_hint: Type the entity ID if your device is not listed (e.g. notify.mobile_app_...). You can find it under Settings → Devices → your phone → Notify entity.
notifications.cooldown_hint: Minimum time between repeated alerts per room
notifications.mold_prevention_notify_hin: Also send a notification when prevention activates (temperature raised)
heat_source.toggle_hint: When this room has both radiator thermostats and an AC/heat pump, RoomMind intelligently routes heating demand to the most efficient device based on temperature gap and outdoor conditions.
heat_source.primary_delta_hint: Only activate the primary source when the temperature gap exceeds this value. Below this threshold, only the fast secondary source is used.
heat_source.outdoor_threshold_hint: Above this outdoor temperature, prefer the AC/heat pump (higher efficiency). Below, prefer the gas boiler/radiator.
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor: Min. outdoor temp for AC heating
heat_source.ac_min_outdoor_hint: Disable AC heating entirely below this temperature to protect the heat pump hardware.
devices.type_info: Thermostat for radiator valves and underfloor heating, climate device for anything that cools or heats with air. This decides how RoomMind drives the device.
devices.managed_note: Without a room sensor every device regulates with its own sensor. Setpoint mode and valve control need a temperature sensor in the room.
devices.setpoint_mode_info: Proportional: RoomMind moves the device's setpoint and so controls how hard it heats or cools. Direct: the device gets the room's target temperature and regulates on its own.
devices.setpoint_offset_info: Added to the room target before it goes to the device. If the device reads 2 degrees colder than your room sensor, enter -2.
devices.idle_info_trv: What the thermostat gets when the room needs no heat. Low setpoint keeps it at its minimum instead of off, for wireless thermostats that fall asleep when off and then miss commands.
devices.idle_info_ac: Turn off switches the device off. Fan only keeps the fan running. Setback leaves it on and moves the setpoint 2 °C away from the room target, e.g. for multi-split systems.
devices.idle_fan_mode_info: Fan speed while the idle device only runs its fan.
devices.setback_auto_off_info: Switches the device off when it had nothing to do for an hour and RoomMind does not need it in the next hour either. Works once the room model is trained.
devices.valve_direct_info: RoomMind sets the valve opening itself, e.g. to 30 %, instead of opening the valve fully. That is quieter and more even. Off: the thermostat controls the valve again.
devices.valve_opening_info: The number entity Home Assistant uses to set the valve opening, e.g. valve_opening_degree. Leave it empty to hand the valve back to the thermostat.
devices.valve_closing_info: Holds the valve at the set opening, whatever the thermostat wants, e.g. valve_closing_degree. Filled in automatically when it is named like the opening degree.
devices.valve_idle_opening_info: The valve opening while the thermostat is not heating, e.g. idle_valve_position in Zigbee2MQTT.
devices.valve_closing_mode_info: Most thermostats have a closing degree, e.g. the SONOFF TRVZB. The SONOFF TRV-ZBT has an idle opening instead. Pick the wrong one and its valve stays open when the room needs no heat.
devices.valve_protection_exclude_info: Valve protection then leaves this valve alone. Useful for entities without a real valve, e.g. a virtual boiler.
devices.coil_dry_info: After cooling the device runs its fan for a while without cooling, so the coil dries and does not get musty. Global follows the evaporator drying setting.
devices.coil_dry_minutes_info: How long the device runs its fan after cooling. 0 uses the global value ({minutes} min).
devices.coil_dry_mode_info: fan_only runs just the fan and almost always fits. Only pick dry if your unit's dry mode is mostly fan, otherwise the compressor cools the coil down again.
devices.coil_dry_fan_mode_info: Fan speed while drying. "Keep current speed" leaves the fan as it is.
devices.heating_system_type_scope: Applies to all thermostats in this room.
roomcard.name: RoomMind room
roomcard.description: Room status with temporary override, mode and comfort/eco temperatures.
roomcard.no_area: Choose a room in the card settings.
roomcard.unknown_room: This room is not set up in RoomMind yet.
roomcard.editor.hide_mode: Hide mode (auto, heat only, cool only)
analytics.zoom_hint: Drag across the chart to zoom, Ctrl + scroll to zoom in steps, Shift + scroll to move.
analytics.zoom_hint_touch: Pinch to zoom, then move with one finger.
analytics.overshoot_heat: then avg. {value} over target, at most {max}
analytics.overshoot_cool: then avg. {value} under target, at most {max}
settings.intro.price: Rooms heat and cool a little more while electricity is cheap and a little less while it is expensive.
settings.price_entity_hint: A price sensor (Tibber, Nordpool, EPEX Spot, aWATTar, ENTSO-e, Octopus or a template). With a forecast attribute (raw_today/raw_tomorrow, data, prices, …) RoomMind can heat ahead of expensive hours; without one it ranks the current price against the last days. Or a switch that is on while energy is cheap (PV surplus, off-peak tariff): it counts as cheap while on. The unit does not matter, only cheap versus expensive.
settings.price_unreadable: The price source has no usable value right now. Rooms keep their schedule until it does.
settings.price_kind_history: no forecast, ranked against the last {hours} h
settings.price_kind_history_learning: no forecast, collecting prices ({hours} of {needed} h)

settings.load_error: The settings could not be loaded. Nothing is changed until they load.
settings.price_room_hint: Pick the price source here. How far the target may move is set per room (schedule settings of the room); rooms without that choice are not affected.
settings.orphans_restore_hint: Create the area again under its original name and the room continues where it left off. Delete a room here if you no longer need it.
settings.intro.coil_dry: Keeps the fan running after cooling so the heat exchanger dries and does not start to smell.
analytics.stage_data_sub: Watch idle times and heating or cooling runs
analytics.stage_learn_sub: Heat loss, heating and cooling power, sun
analytics.stage_control_sub: Plans ahead: starts in time, does not overshoot
analytics.stage_control_simple: Off: simple on/off control is selected in the settings
analytics.stage_control_managed: Needs a temperature sensor in the room; until then the device controls itself
sensors.temp_info: With a sensor RoomMind measures the room itself and tells the devices when to heat or cool (Full Control). Without one the devices regulate with their own sensor (Managed).
sensors.full_control_note: Full Control: RoomMind regulates by this sensor. Without it the devices regulate on their own again.
sensors.humidity_info: Shows the humidity and is needed for the mold warning. Without a sensor the room gets no mold warning.
sensors.window_info: While a window or door is open, RoomMind pauses heating and cooling in this room.
sensors.window_open_delay_info: How long a window has to be open before RoomMind pauses. A short opening then interrupts nothing.
sensors.window_close_delay_info: How long RoomMind waits after closing before it heats or cools again.
sensors.occupancy_info: Motion or presence sensors in the room. RoomMind uses them to learn how much heat people add and can switch an empty room to eco.
sensors.occupancy_eco_info: When all sensors report the room empty for longer than the delay, eco applies until someone is back. The room then only warms up once someone is in it. Override, vacation and presence come first.
sensors.occupancy_eco_delay_info: How long all sensors have to report nothing before eco applies (5 to 240 minutes).
